Author: Ilesh J. Vora
Bench: Ilesh J. Vora
 R/Scr.A/8297/2022 Order

DATED: 21/02/2023  R/SPECIAL CRIMINAL APPLICATION NO. 8297 of 2022 ==========================================================
 DEVILAL HARIJILAL SUTHAR  Versus

Appearance:
MR BHAVIK R SAMANI(8339) for the petitioner(s) No. 1 for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MR JK SHAH, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ILESH J. VORA  Date : 21/02/2023
ORAL ORDER 1.

By way of this petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the petitioner original complainant seeking transfer of investigation of the FIR being C.R.No.81/2019 registered on 20.07.2019 with Oldpad Police Station, Surat.

2. Facts and circumstances giving rise to filing present application are that, pursuant to the FIR,
allegedly registered for the offence punishable under Sections 406, 420, 120 (b) and 114 of IPC against the accused namely Hasmukh Bed, Milan Bhambhar and Bhura Dhinaiya, the police officer of Olpad Police Station have not taken any step to investigate the matter and till date, the accused are not arrested.

The accused have floated the scheme of flats at Surat and after receiving the substantial amount from the complainant as well as other buyers, did not have completed the construction work of the flats and diverted the amount of sale consideration to the other firms namely Dhanraj Developers and withdrew the same for their personal purpose.
It is further alleged that, the accused have without completing the construction of flats left the construction site and fled away.

The accused have executed the same modus at the different cities of Gujarat and duped innocent investors and thereby, committed the offence of cheating R/SCR.A/8297/2022 ORDER DATED: 21/02/2023 and criminal breach of trust.
The complainant made a representation to the higher police officials either directly IO to make fair and proper investigation or to transfer the investigation to independent agency.
However, there has been no progress in the matter.
As per the facts of the FIR and material placed on record, this scam amounting to Rs.10 crores and more.

sentences.text: 3. In the aforesaid facts, the instant application has been preferred by the original informant for issuance necessary direction to transfer the investigation to an independent agency.
4. Mr. B. R. Samani, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that, since registration of the FIR, there has been no any substantial progress in investigation.
The scam amounting to more than Rs.10 crore affecting society at large, investigation having not been seriously investigated as the accused are influenced persons.

Thus, if the investigation is transferred to any independent agency,
then no prejudice will cause to the prosecution and on the other hand, if investigation is allowed to be continued, then there is all possibilities there there would be serious prejudice caused to the right of the complainant for fair investigation.

Thus, looking to the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case, learned counsel would submit that, case is made out for exercise inherent powers of this Court for transferring investigation as prayed for.
5.

Learned State counsel Mr. J.K.Shah would submit that there is no justification to transfer the case to any other independent agency and therefore, no case is made out for exercising inherent powers of this Court.
Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the present case, since 2019, there is no substantial progress in the investigation.

Considering the allegations levelled in the FIR and subsequent registration of FIRs against the accused, this Court is of considered view that, the allegations made against the accused are serious one and are affecting society at large as innocent persons have been duped.

In Ramlal Narang Vs. State (Delhi Administration) [AIR 79 SC 1791], it was observed by the Apex Court that, in the normal circumstances, investigation of criminal case carried out by the State agency, could not be subject matter of judicial review in the writ jurisdiction of the High Court, but where special facts and circumstances are involved, thereby the right of any citizen have been violated by the authorities can certainly high Court has jurisdiction to pass necessary direction.

sentences.text: It is settled proposition of law that justice should not only be done, but it should be appeared that the same is being done.
7. Having regard to the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case and considering the stage of investigation, case is made out to exercise inherent powers of this Court.

Accordingly,
investigation of the case is hereby transferred and entrusted to Dy.S.P., Surat Rural, who shall complete the investigation within four months from the date of receipt of this order in accordance with law.
With these observations and direction, present petition is disposed of in the above terms.
